recipe.name: Char Siu Pork Belly in Traditional Homemade Marinade (No Colour)
directions: Scrub the pork belly clean using some flour as abrasive. Wash and rinse multiple times until the water runs clear. Pat dry completely.
Remove the skin, and divide the pork in 5-cm-thick strips or sections.
Prick the meat to allow the marinade to seep in.
Mix all the ingredients of the marinade together. Massage it into the meat.
Transfer to an airtight container, and let it marinate for at least 24 hours in the fridge. If you intend to cook this at a later date, store it in the freezer. It'll keep for months!
When you are ready to cook, take the meat out of the freezer and let it defrost completely.
Lay it out on a foil-lined baking tray, and cook in a 180°C oven for 40 mins.
While the pork is cooking in the oven, prepare the basting liquid and the glaze.
_For the basting liquid_: Transfer any leftover marinade to a small bowl. Microwave it for 1 minute. Set aside.

_For the glaze_: In a saucepan, add the rock sugar, water and oil, and cook until the sugar dissolves and turns slightly brown. Squeeze in some lime juice to check crystallisation. Remove in a small bowl and set aside. It will become thick and sticky as it cools.
Once the pork is out of the oven, baste it and place it back in the oven at 150°C for 15 mins.
After that, take the tray out once again, brush on the glaze, and put it back in the oven one last time at 200°C for just 2 mins until the top is glassy.
Allow it to cool slightly before slicing. Serve with fresh greens like lettuce, cucumber or blanched bok choy.
